table_title: List the major modern epidemics and pandemics from 1918 (Spanish flu) through 2025 — the union of (a) Wikipedia 'List of epidemics and pandemics' master-article Major-by-death-toll list filtered to start-year ≥ 1918, (b) Wikipedia master-article Ongoing-pandemics list, and (c) WHO-declared Public Health Emergencies of International Concern — with the start year, causal pathogen or disease, affected region, primary transmission mode, and a brief specific trigger description.
db_analog: SELECT epidemic, start_year, disease, affected_region, transmission_mode, specific_trigger FROM modern_epidemics_and_pandemics WHERE start_year >= 1918 AND (event_in_major_by_death_toll_top19 = TRUE OR event_in_ongoing_pandemics_list = TRUE OR event_in_who_pheic_declarations = TRUE) ORDER BY start_year, epidemic
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of epidemics and pandemics' master article + Wikipedia 'Public health emergency of international concern' article, both accessed 2026-05-13. Universe is the 16 major modern epidemics and pandemics from 1918 (1918 influenza pandemic) through 2025 (the most recent Sudanese cholera epidemic entry in the master article's Ongoing-pandemics list) that satisfy at least one of three authoritative-master rules: (a) the event is in the master article's 'Major epidemics and pandemics by death toll' top-19 list (Table[0] per pandas.read_html) AND has start-year ≥ 1918 (6 candidate memberships: 1918 Spanish flu, 1918-1922 Russia typhus epidemic, 1957-1958 Asian flu, 1968-1970 Hong Kong flu, HIV/AIDS pandemic 1981-present, COVID-19 pandemic 2019-present); (b) the event is in the master article's 'Ongoing pandemics' list (Table[8] per pandas.read_html — 6 events: Seventh cholera pandemic 1961-present, HIV/AIDS pandemic 1981-present, MERS outbreak 2012-present, COVID-19 pandemic 2019-present, 2023-2026 monkeypox epidemic 2023-present, 2024-2025 Sudanese cholera epidemic 2024-present); (c) the event has a formal WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern declaration (8 PHEIC declarations since 2009: 2009-2010 H1N1 swine flu pandemic, 2014 polio declaration (ongoing), 2013-2016 Western African Ebola virus epidemic, 2015-2016 Zika virus epidemic, 2018-2020 Kivu Ebola epidemic, 2020-2023 COVID-19 declaration, 2022-2023 mpox outbreak Clade IIb, 2024 mpox PHEIC continuation Clade Ib captured by the chronological table's '2023-2026 monkeypox epidemic' entry). After dedup across the three sets (HIV/AIDS appears in (a)+(b); COVID-19 appears in (a)+(b)+(c); both mpox PHEIC declarations are captured by the two chronological-table mpox entries: '2022-2023 mpox outbreak' for Clade IIb and '2023-2026 monkeypox epidemic' for Clade Ib), the universe contains 16 unique events. Per-row cells: Epidemic name verbatim from the master article's Event column (Tables[5-8] for chronological-table events; for the 2014 polio PHEIC the canonical-form name is '2014 polio declaration' per the PHEIC article's heading phrasing, since the chronological-table list does not have a dedicated entry); Start Year is the 4-digit integer first year of the master Years column (e.g., 'Hong Kong flu' Years='1968-1970' is staged as Year 1968; '2022-2023 mpox outbreak' is staged as Year 2022); Disease is verbatim from the master article's Disease column where available (otherwise from the PHEIC Wikipedia article's pathogen identifier); Affected Region is normalized to a 6-value continent-or-global vocabulary (Worldwide / Africa / Americas / Asia / Europe / Oceania) — single-continent events use the continent (Russia → Europe; DRC+Uganda → Africa; Sudan+SS+Chad → Africa); multi-continent or 'Worldwide, primarily X' events use 'Worldwide' per the source's primary framing; Transmission Mode is a curator-derived 5-value closed taxonomy (Respiratory / Vector-borne / Direct contact / Water-or-Food-borne / Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism) describing the primary epidemiological transmission mechanism — the closed taxonomy maps to canonical WHO/CDC pathogen-transmission categories and tests causal-mechanism attribution; Specific Trigger is a 1-line curator paraphrase (12-22 words) of the documented spillover event, contamination source, or causal narrative for each event. The 16-row universe is moderately stable on a multi-year horizon: future entries to the Ongoing-pandemics list (a major 2026+ pandemic) would extend the universe; future PHEIC declarations would also extend; the 2014 polio PHEIC is still in force as of 2026.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `causal` gap-1 saturation gap (causal at gap 1 with 4 of 5 target staged before this instance; this instance brings it to 5/5 SATURATING the category — FOURTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection, set_operation, set_filter). User-selected via deep-dive on schema design from 3 schema alternatives (A: 4 cols all exact-match; B: 5 cols mirroring financial-crises; C: 6 cols adding pathogen specificity) and 3 universe alternatives (A: Master+Ongoing 10 rows; B: Master+Ongoing+PHEIC 14-16 rows; C: chronological-table threshold 25+ rows). User picked Schema C + Universe B + anchor year 1918. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 18 — 2 master + 16 per-event articles. The master 'List of epidemics and pandemics' article supplies 15 of 16 Epidemic/Year/Disease/Region cells via its chronological-tables wikitable (Tables[0,5,6,7,8] in pandas.read_html order); the master 'Public health emergency of international concern' Wikipedia article supplies the canonical PHEIC declaration list (8 declarations) used to identify the 2014 polio declaration entry which has no dedicated chronological-table row. The 16 per-event Wikipedia articles (1 per row; for the Russia typhus 1918 row which lacks a dedicated event article, the per-pathogen 'Epidemic typhus' article supplies the transmission and trigger information) ground the Transmission Mode and Specific Trigger answer-key cells: each event's dedicated Wikipedia article's Transmission / Etiology / Origin / Lead sections support the staged Transmission Mode value (from the closed 5-value taxonomy) and the Specific Trigger paraphrase (12-22-word lead-summary of the documented spillover or causal narrative). Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited master Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse tables[0] (Major by death toll, top-19), tables[5-7] (chronological 1800-2024), tables[8] (Ongoing pandemics, 6 rows), (3) filter Table[0] to start-year ≥ 1918 (yields 6 candidate memberships including HIV/AIDS and COVID-19), union with Table[8] (yields 6 ongoing events with HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 deduping against Table[0]), union with the 8 WHO PHEIC declarations from the PHEIC article (with COVID-19 deduping against Table[0]+Table[8] and the two mpox PHEIC declarations captured by the two chronological-table mpox entries) (yields 2009 swine flu, 2014 polio, 2013-16 W. Africa Ebola, 2015-16 Zika, 2018-20 Kivu Ebola, COVID-19 [dedup], 2022-23 mpox, 2024 mpox [captured by 2023-2026 monkeypox entry]), (4) for each row take Epidemic name verbatim from the chronological-table Event column (the 2014 polio PHEIC uses '2014 polio declaration' as a constructed name from the PHEIC article's framing), Start Year as 4-digit integer first year of Years column, Disease verbatim from the Disease column (or PHEIC article's pathogen identifier for polio), Affected Region normalized to 6-value continent-or-global vocabulary, Transmission Mode curator-derived from 5-value closed taxonomy, Specific Trigger as 12-22-word curator paraphrase of documented spillover/contamination/causal narrative. Result: 16 rows × 6 columns, PK on Epidemic, 0 duplicates. Transmission Mode distribution (16 rows): Respiratory 6 (Spanish flu, Asian flu, Hong Kong flu, 2009 swine flu, MERS, COVID-19), Direct contact 5 (HIV/AIDS, West African Ebola, Kivu Ebola, 2022 mpox, 2023-26 monkeypox), Water-or-Food-borne 3 (Seventh cholera, 2014 polio, 2024 Sudanese cholera), Vector-borne 2 (Russia typhus, Zika), Iatrogenic-or-Bioterrorism 0 (no events in the universe under this closed-vocabulary value). Affected Region distribution: Worldwide 13, Africa 2 (Kivu Ebola, 2024 Sudanese cholera), Europe 1 (Russia typhus); the heavily-Worldwide distribution reflects the modern-pandemic-scale nature of the universe (Major-by-death-toll, Ongoing-pandemics, and PHEIC all favour global-spread events). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical pandemics (1918 Spanish flu, HIV/AIDS, 2009 swine flu, COVID-19); mid-difficulty cells include the major modern outbreaks (1957 Asian flu, 1968 Hong Kong flu, 2002-2004 SARS [not in universe], 2014 W. Africa Ebola, 2015 Zika); harder calibration cells include the less-headline-grabbing events (Russia typhus 1918, Seventh cholera pandemic, 2014 polio PHEIC, Kivu Ebola, 2022 mpox Clade IIb vs 2023 Clade Ib distinction, 2024 Sudanese cholera). The closed Transmission Mode taxonomy tests whether the LLM can correctly classify each event into the 5-value epidemiological vocabulary; the most challenging cases are events with multiple transmission modes (HIV/AIDS has sexual + bloodborne + mother-to-child; staged as 'Direct contact' per the dominant primary mode) and events where transmission mode differs from origin (Spanish flu has indeterminate geographic origin per its per-event source but human-to-human transmission-mode 'Respiratory'). Specific Trigger cells are 1-line curator paraphrases (12-22 words each) drawn from canonical epidemiological knowledge backed by Wikipedia per-event articles; they preserve the proximate-cause specificity that the closed Transmission Mode taxonomy abstracts away (e.g., 'H1N1 pandemic spread from probable early U.S. cases through WWI-era troop movements; geographic origin remains uncertain' is more specific than just 'Respiratory'). Notable exclusions documented for cycle-1 audit: SARS 2002-2004 is iconic but excluded by strict Option B rule (not in Table[0] top-19, not in Table[8] ongoing, not formally PHEIC-declared since PHEIC declarations started in 2009); other notable exclusions are 1976 first Ebola outbreak (pre-PHEIC era and not in top-19/ongoing), 1979 Sverdlovsk anthrax leak (small scale, not in top-19), 1994 plague in India (not in top-19/ongoing/PHEIC). Cycle-1 audit may surface these and the curator-derived 2014 polio PHEIC row name as risk areas needing source-grounding clarification.
